Its workflow reconstructions explicitly withhold identities, addresses, access details, correspondence, and participant-level records.

NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC visibly joins civic participation, place, technical implementation, and documentary attention: cultural-space meetings, safety and legal sessions, town halls, hearings, campaign sites, source maps, minutes, action trackers, and decision records connect public rooms to maintained digital surfaces. The case repeatedly limits Jamie’s contribution, preserves collective campaign credit, and disclaims sole causation.

WOWList visibly connects artistic and social scenes to technical product practice: Jamie and Richard Caceres co-built a natural-language, collaboratively editable community-calendar system across 35 city ecosystems, translating organizers’ own vocabulary into publishing, discovery, digests, embeds, and distribution workflows while crediting organizers and protecting private user data.

Knowledge Wiki Graphs makes attention and care operational through a recursive sequence—observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document for continuation—while distinguishing known, open, and protected material and requiring human review.

The rushed-reader path remains role-legible: the homepage identifies Jamie as a Technical Project Manager focused on Product Operations and Implementation; the dedicated Technical Operations page foregrounds requirements, delivery rhythms, risk signals, QA/UAT, launch support, onboarding, documentation, and handoffs; the public resume reinforces this target.
